author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: However little known the feelings or views of such a man may be on his first entering a neighbourhood, this truth is so well fixed in the minds of the surrounding families, that he is considered the rightful property of some one or other of their daughters.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: “My dear Mr. Bennet,” said his lady to him one day, “have you heard that Netherfield Park is let at last?”

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: Mr. Bennet replied that he had not.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: “But it is,” returned she; “for Mrs. Long has just been here, and she told me all about it.”

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: “Do you not want to know who has taken it?” cried his wife impatiently.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: “You want to tell me, and I have no objection to hearing it.”

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: “Why, my dear, you must know, Mrs. Long says that Netherfield is taken by a young man of large fortune from the north of England; that he came down on Monday in a chaise and four to see the place...”
